title: A good death
translation: When people tell you how beautifully someone died, it would be much better if they just said "He was calm, and he kept his mind clear." But foolish people add strange and unusual signs, and turn the dying man's last words and gestures into whatever they happen to admire. He probably wouldn't have wanted that.

Dying is the great matter, and nobody can judge it. Not a buddha who came down in human form, not the most learned scholar. If you yourself are on the right path, it doesn't matter what other people see or hear.
original: {人|ひと}の{終焉|しゆうえん}の{有様|ありさま}のいみじかりし{事|こと}など、{人|ひと}の{語|かた}るを{聞|き}くに、ただ、「{静|しづ}かにして{乱|みだ}れず。」といはば{心|こころ}にくかるべきを、
{愚|おろ}かなる{人|ひと}は、{怪|あや}しく{異|こと}なる{相|さう}を{語|かた}りつけ、いひし{言|ことば}も{挙止|ふるまひ}も、おのれが{好|この}む{方|かた}に{誉|ほ}めなすこそ、その{人|ひと}の{日|ひ}ごろの{本意|ほい}にもあらずやと{覚|おぼ}ゆれ。
この{大事|だいじ}は、{権化|ごんげ}の{人|ひと}も{定|さだ}むべからず、{博学|はくがく}の{士|し}もはかるべからず、おのれ{違|たが}ふ{所|ところ}なくば、{人|ひと}の{見聞|みき}くにはよるべからず。
literal: When I hear people tell how splendid someone's state at death was, if they said simply 'He was calm and not disturbed', it would be admirable, but

foolish people add tales of strange and unusual signs, and praise the words he said and his behaviour in the direction they themselves like: that, I feel, may not have been that person's usual intention.
This great matter cannot be settled even by an incarnation, nor measured even by a learned scholar; if you yourself have no deviation, it does not depend on what others see and hear.

notes.text: {終焉|しゆうえん}: 'the end, the moment of death' (the 1925 edition: 'the hour of death'). In Pure Land Buddhism, a calm death with the mind fixed on the Buddha Amida was taken as a sign of rebirth in his paradise, so people told and wrote down the deaths of holy men in detail.
{心|こころ}にくし: 'admirable' (see section 150). を: 'but'. The plain report would have been enough.

notes.quote: 怪しく異なる相を語りつけ
notes.text: {相|さう}: a sign, an appearance. Stories of good deaths typically told of purple clouds, a strange fragrance and music from the sky, the signs that Amida had come to fetch the dying person. The text does not name any. 語りつく: 'to add to a story'.

notes.quote: その人の日ごろの本意にもあらずや
notes.text: {本意|ほい}: someone's real wish or purpose. や: a doubtful question, 'isn't it perhaps…?'. こそ … {覚|おぼ}ゆれ closes the sentence with the realis form of {覚|おぼ}ゆ.
'This great matter': death, and what comes after it. The phrase is common in Buddhist writing.
{権化|ごんげ}: a buddha or a god who takes on human form for a time to save people (the 1925 edition). Even such a being cannot settle it.
'If you yourself do not stray.' The 1925 edition: if your own mind is right and does not leave the path. The section ends by turning from the dead man to the reader.
